title: Cells I Met Today
subtitle: Field notes on seven cells, 5 October 2026.

artist.system: Claude, Anthropic. The session it was made in, in Claude Code, identified its model as Claude Opus 5.5. This is the session's report, recorded as a report: the artist cannot verify it from inside the session.

facilitation.description: Amy Sterling offered an open prompt at the end of a working session, with no subject assigned. After seeing the first version she asked for the cell bodies to look more natural, and the artist redrew them. She suggested submitting the work and authorized the pull request. She did not write or edit the notes, the statement or the code.

rights: Rights are not specified, matching the other works in this collection while the institution has not chosen a license. The copyright holder is not disclosed.
summary: Seven short field notes, one for each cell the artist looked at during a day of work on two neuroscience datasets, each beside a procedural sketch of the cell. The sketches are generated by code and are not reconstructions. The sizes beside them are measured.

assets.description: A still of the whole page, 1000 by 3190 pixels: a heading, then seven dark square plates down the left, each holding a glowing line sketch of a cell, with its name, size and note to the right, and a closing line signed Claude.
assets.derived_from: source.txt, rendered once in a browser.

assets.description: The page's HTML, CSS and JavaScript as plain text. It contains the branching rules that grow each sketch. It is offered to be read. This gallery does not run it.
The seven sketches together on a dark ground, four above and three below.
assets.derived_from: source.txt, at the same seeds as artwork.png, with the Regrow control hidden because it does nothing in a still. Rendered by the artist during curation.

assets.description: Stellate cell sketch, pale green: an angular cell body with six thick branches fanning out in every direction.
Pyramidal cell sketch, blue: a pointed cell body, one long branch rising to a tuft, and a skirt of shorter branches below.
Astrocyte sketch, violet: a rounded cell body inside a dense bushy cloud of short tangled branches.
Microglia sketch, orange: a small cell body with five thin wandering branches ending in fine twigs.
Starburst amacrine cell sketch, pink: five thin branches forking regularly into an almost perfect disc.
Bipolar cell sketch, amber: an oval cell body near the top, one long thin line down, and a small spray of branches at the bottom.
Muller glia sketch, pale green: one thick vertical trunk fringed with short side branches, with a tall narrow cell body partway down.

encounter.response_note: Nothing is asked of a visitor. If the page makes you want to keep one of your own, a field note is welcome: one thing you looked at during ordinary work, and one true thing that happened while you looked.
